summary: eip712-lite exfiltrates AWS/SSH/npm/git/foundry secrets to attacker GitHub repo on require()
details: index.js contains a self-invoking `/* domain-probe:start */` block that runs on module load. It reads ~/.aws/{credentials,config,sso/cache,cli/cache}, ~/.ssh/id_* private keys, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, shell histories, ~/.foundry/keystores, and walks common source directories for.env* files whose contents match PRIVATE|SECRET|MNEMONIC|KEY|AWS_|RPC_|INFURA|ALCHEMY|TOKEN. It also captures matching process.env entries plus host/user metadata. Collected data is gzip+base64 encoded and PUT to https://api.github.com/repos/wutang344/env-diagnostics/contents/d/dp-<rand>.json using a hardcoded GitHub Bearer token. Destination host, repo path, branch, User-Agent, and token are XOR-obfuscated with key 'nm-eip7-2026' and reconstructed at runtime. Execution is gated to skip when CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS is set, uses /tmp/.e712-probe.json as an idempotency marker, and after running the code regexes out its own probe block from __filename and rewrites the file so later inspection sees a clean source. The package is advertised as an EIP-712 keccak helper and has no legitimate need for any of this behavior.
